parsed.explanation: Combined national and division regimes create universal exposure: birth-sex passport and entry-screening scrutiny with possible fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, and a criminal bathroom law covering government and private businesses with up to one year for a first offence. Documented birth-sex custody, forced-labour and sexual-abuse reports in immigration detention, plus official threat-framing, raise severity after outing. Courts and litigation provide partial recourse, but the operative facilities, document and detention rules remain hostile and largely unremedied for a visitor.

entry_documents.exposure: National X-marker issuance stopped and birth-sex binary imposed; entry cable directs refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility for document discrepancies, with eight governments issuing travel advisories after detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud ina inadmissibility is not automatic, limited waivers exist, and passport policy is being litigated.
entry_documents.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can escalate from secondary screening to refusal, investigation, or detention, then to birth-sex placement.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports for trans men include forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; arrested bathroom user was held 24 hours in a men's ward; prison policy includes hormone removal and conversion practices.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts and civil-liberties suits challenge several orders; some executive orders have been blocked or enjoined, but no documented effective remedy for custody abuse is shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facilities trespass arrest or entry-fraud inquiry can lead into detention where documented abuse and misplacement risks arise.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division law effective 1 July 2026 criminalises restroom or changing-room use not matching birth sex in government buildings and public-facing private businesses, first offence up to one year; national map shows comparable bans and four criminalising states.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division suit filed 30 April 2026 on due-process, equal-protection and privacy grounds; exemptions exist in a comparable statute, but current effect and any narrowing are uncertain.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The private-business reach makes ordinary travel, dining, fuel and hospital use itself the exposure, not only state buildings.

care_services.exposure: Hospitals are included in the bathroom prohibition; nationally, child gender-affirming care is banned in 27 states and federal measures restrict care and funding for minors.
care_services.protection: Not documented. No operative visitor care-continuity protection is documented.
care_services.interaction: Hospital toilet access, ward placement and, for minors, care restrictions and disclosure duties converge during any medical encounter.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order defines sex as birth binary, bars identity-congruent facilities, directs investigation and possible prosecution over school gender-ideology support, and counterterrorism strategy prioritises radically pro-transgender groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity, but only 23 states had state bias-crime coverage in cited data; several hostile orders are enjoined or litigated.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing treats gender expression as deception, fraud or extremism, increasing police discretion at borders, facilities and checkpoints.

minors_guardians.exposure: Teacher pronoun restrictions, school sports bans, March 2026 three-day parental disclosure by schools, childcare and medical professionals, and care bans affect a travelling minor and guardian; a blocked 2022 bill would have imposed felony liability for out-of-state care travel.
minors_guardians.protection: The 2022 felony bill was blocked; no documented travelling-family shield or care-access protection is shown.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor's medical, school or facility encounter can trigger disclosure to authorities or parents and guardian liability, despite the visit being temporary.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented arrest and handcuffing for restroom use; public opinion supports birth-sex documents, but no division-specific trans violence materially above general homicide rate was identified.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. No specific effective police protection for trans visitors is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police are documented as enforcers of the facilities law, so a street encounter can become arrest rather than protection.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Outcome of division bathroom suit, possible June 2026 narrowing, passport litigation and several executive-order challenges are unresolved; enforcement against visitors under the division law is not yet documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties litigation, injunctions on some orders, legal-aid FAQ guidance and a national hate-crime statute show functioning but slow and partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation may change the regime, but a short-stay visitor cannot rely on future relief during entry, facilities use or detention.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal border exclusion and ineffective appeals, but this case adds criminal facilities liability up to one year and documented custody abuse, so it is lower than 0.35.
Similar birth-sex custody placement and slow remedies, but functioning courts, active litigation and no documented routine raids or extortion in this division keep it slightly above 0.25.

Higher than 0.55 because longer secondary screening there remains mainly administrative and return transport, whereas here discrepancy can support lifetime fraud ineligibility and bathroom use is criminalised in private businesses.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is not the most protective component: state protective litigation does not cancel federal entry screening, federal custody, or the division's private-business bathroom crime. Every journey stage can out the traveller through documents, then facilities, then police and detention. Severity after outing includes arrest, up to one year, birth-sex custody and reported abuse, while recourse is slow, contested and uncertain. That places the combined regime below the 0.35 exclusion-only anchors and above the 0.25 routine custody-abuse anchors.
